specDepartures.evidence: Deleting `issuePod.affinity` (podkind.go:189-219) removes the only rule that forced trees apart; the scheduler and Karpenter bin-pack pending pods into the fewest nodes the pool's requirements allow, so node count is an outcome of instance sizes the repository does not control, not of this change.

acceptance: Acceptance 1: 'shows them on at least two nodes' becomes 'carry no affinity and may land on any nodes the pool has room on; the run records their nodes and asserts two or more only when the pool's instance requirements make two pods not fit one node'

specDepartures.plan: The proof asserts what the change guarantees: no `affinity` in any of the three pod specs, three distinct Bound PVCs selected by `legion.dev/issue`, and a sibling's workspace path unreadable from another issue's pod; it records `kubectl get pod -o wide` and asserts 'at least two nodes' only when the preflight's read of the `legion` NodePool shows no allowed instance can hold two of the run's pods.
specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: a root and two of its children run at once; `kubectl get pod -o wide` shows them on at least two nodes, each with its own PersistentVolumeClaim, and no pod can read another issue's workspace.

specDepartures.evidence: A gVisor pod exposes no /sys/fs/cgroup files (measured in the planner's own pod: nproc 8, MemTotal 62 GiB, no cpu.max or memory.max); runsc derives the sandbox's CPU count and total memory from the pod cgroup (runsc/sandbox/sandbox.go:1408-1428 with --cpu-num-from-quota default true, floor 2, config/flags.go:117) and a multi-container sandbox's per-container cgroup 'makes no change to the container' (runsc/container/container.go:129-136).

acceptance: Acceptance 2: 'inside a pod the cgroup CPU quota and memory limit match them' becomes 'inside a pod nproc and MemTotal equal the pod's summed CPU and memory limits, as gVisor derives them from the pod cgroup; per-container values are checked from the API'

specDepartures.plan: Inside a pod the check is `nproc == max(2, ceil(sum of the pod's CPU limits))` and `/proc/meminfo` MemTotal within 3% of the sum of the pod's memory limits; each container's own request and limit, and `status.qosClass == Guaranteed`, are read from the Kubernetes API.
specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 2: inside a pod the cgroup CPU quota and memory limit match them (the configured requests and limits).

specDepartures.evidence: Neither path the spec names can release a done child's volume while its tree is live: the orphan sweep keeps every Sandbox of a live tree (sandbox.go:752-810) and a closed child's suspended claims stay known; the tree's close comes at the root's linger expiry (workflow/linger.go:90-114). Acceptance 3 requires the release while the parent's pod and volume stay, so the child's own close effect (sandbox/issue_suspend.go:20-57, store/issue_suspend.go:33-101) does it; a retired claim with a recorded session would otherwise resume into a missing file and report a lost volume (outbox.go:544-553, workspace_init.go:244-246).

summary: 'Whole-tree close and orphan cleanup release each issue's volume when that issue is done' becomes 'a child's close as done releases its volume at once and retires its roles; the tree's close and the orphan sweep release every other issue's volume'

specDepartures.plan: A child that leaves the workflow as `done` releases its own volume at once: its claims are retired with their session records cleared and its Sandbox is foreground-deleted by the close's durable effect, so a later `todo` re-enters it fresh. A child parked in backlog, icebox or triage keeps its suspended Sandbox and volume until the tree closes. The tree's close and the orphan sweep release the rest, each Sandbox now taking its own volume.
specDepartures.spec: Whole-tree close and orphan cleanup release each issue's volume when that issue is done, with the lifetime rules the runtime has today for the tree volume moved to the issue.

specDepartures.evidence: relaunch.go:539-611 and podkind.go:221-281, cmd/legion/workspace_init.go:38,44-61,270-273,300-423,486 and internal/daemon/removable.go exist only for a shared clone; internal/api/version.go:9-17,43-46 puts LEGION_REMOVABLE_WORKSPACES under the contract; internal/daemon/kubernetes.go:114-119 sets no probe resources while acceptance 2 says every Legion pod; config/kubernetes.go:30-33,60-64 hold the tree-volume and requests/limits shapes; docs/kubernetes.md:482-568 is #1752's cutover.

outcome.scope: Adds the deletion of the shared-disk machinery, the contract bump, the probe pod's reservation, the issue_volume and flat resources config keys, and the boot census rule; the deployment's legion.yaml changes in the same cutover.

specDepartures.plan: The plan also deletes the machinery that existed only because a tree's issues shared one disk (the tree launch turn, workspace-init's repository flock and LEGION_WORKSPACE_INIT_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS, the removable-workspaces pipeline and its docs), bumps DaemonAPIVersion 15 to 16, gives the image probe pod the controller's reservation, renames tree_volume to issue_volume, flattens resources.<role> to {cpu, memory}, and adds a boot census rule refusing a tree-volume-layout Sandbox so this lands only in #1752's drained cutover.
specDepartures.spec: The spec's four 'What changes' bullets: per-issue volume, no affinity, reservations with defaults and overrides, docs and live proofs.
